cvEn:
Yehoshua Volgelrenter, son of Hava and Israel-Eliezer, was born in 1913 in Poland. As a boy he moved to New York, where he completed his studies at the "Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan" Yeshiva. In New York he came into contact with Hashomer Hatzair and adopted its ideas and aims. In 1934 he immigrated to the Land of Israel and settled in Kibbutz Ein HaShofet. After some time he moved to Jerusalem, where he studied at the Hebrew University and worked to support himself. At that time he married Yehudit, and when their son Uzi was born, his happiness knew no bounds. The whole family later settled in Haifa because of Yehoshua's activity in the Haganah, the pre-state Jewish defense organization. By day he worked to support the family at the Bank of South Africa, and at night he served as a Notar, a member of the Jewish Supernumerary Police.

During the War of Independence, the Haganah appointed him to guard the building that housed the bank after it was damaged in a car bomb explosion. He was always the first to report to his guard post, even though he knew that the place posed great danger to him. On 9 Adar I 5708 (19 February 1948), he fell while carrying out his duties during an attack by murderers, and was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Haifa. He left behind a wife and a son, his mother, four brothers and three sisters.
